B.explanation: Both values are wrong - amplitude is larger than $2 \text{ cm}$ and wave S oscillates faster than wave R, so its period must be less than $30 \text{ ms}$, not $90 \text{ ms}$.

C.explanation: Amplitude is about half of $8 \text{ cm}$, giving $4 \text{ cm}$, and three cycles of S fit in one $30 \text{ ms}$ cycle of R, giving $10 \text{ ms}$.

walkthrough: Identify the given data: wave R has amplitude $x_0 = 8 \text{ cm}$ and period $T_R = 30 \text{ ms}$. Amplitude is the maximum displacement from zero and period is the time for one full oscillation.
Find amplitude of S from peak heights: on the displacement-time graph the peak of wave S is about one half the peak of wave R. So $x_{0,S} \approx 8 \text{ cm} / 2 = 4 \text{ cm}$.
Find period of S by counting cycles: in the time wave R completes one full cycle, wave S completes three full cycles. So wave S has three times the frequency and one third the period.
Calculate: $T_S = T_R / 3 = 30 \text{ ms} / 3 = 10 \text{ ms}$. The unit remains $\text{ms}$ and the shorter time matches the faster oscillation seen.
Combine $4 \text{ cm}$ and $10 \text{ ms}$. This is option C.
